subject: history
title: War of Resistance (1937–45): the war that did not wait for 1939
dek: From the clash at the Marco Polo Bridge to the wartime capital in Chongqing, this is a world war looked at from China, not as Asia’s footnote to Europe.

thumb.alt: Aerial photograph of the Lugou (Marco Polo) Bridge and Wanping fortress.

hero.alt: Aerial view of the Lugou Bridge crossing a wide riverbed beside the walled town of Wanping, with an aircraft nose at the bottom of the frame.
hero.caption: The Lugou (Marco Polo) Bridge and Wanping, southwest of Beiping. On 7–8 July 1937 a clash here became the start of full-scale war between the Republic of China and Japan. The photograph is a later aerial; the geography is the fact.

honesty: This lesson looks out from China. Europe’s 1939 is contemporaneous, not the frame. “World War II” as a 1939–45 European story leaves 1937–39 as a preface. From Chongqing, 1939 is the year the European war caught up. Nanjing is treated with one careful image of a city after bombing — no corpses as illustration. Casualty figures that cannot be sourced here are omitted.

timeline.label: Mukden / Lytton
timeline.detail: Japan seized Manchuria after the Mukden Incident. The League of Nations sent the Lytton Commission. The full-scale war was still ahead.

timeline.label: Lugou / Shanghai
timeline.detail: 7 July at the Marco Polo Bridge; the Battle of Shanghai opened in August and made the war visible to foreign cameras.

timeline.label: Nanjing
timeline.detail: The capital fell in December. Massacre followed. This lesson will not decorate that fact with bodies.

timeline.label: Chongqing
timeline.detail: Wartime capital after the retreat up the Yangtze. Years of bombing. People lived in tunnels.

timeline.label: Europe
timeline.detail: Germany invaded Poland. A second opening of a world war, not the first.

timeline.label: Surrender / after
timeline.detail: Japan surrendered. The Chinese civil war did not wait long. Memory became a second fight between states.

watch.title: The Battle of China (1944) — Why We Fight
watch.note: U.S. Army orientation film, Frank Capra series. Public-domain American wartime framing of the China theater — useful as a primary object, not as a neutral history. Internet Archive.

glossary.explain: Chinese name for the full-scale war with Japan, conventionally dated from 7 July 1937 to 1945. Some Chinese histories include 1931. This capsule uses 1937–45 as the full-scale span and treats 1931 as the before.
Stone bridge over the Yongding River near Wanping, southwest of Beiping. A clash beginning 7 July 1937 became the opening of full-scale war. Europeans had long called it the Marco Polo Bridge.
Walled town at the north end of the Lugou Bridge. The 1937 incident is a fight over a railway town and a crossing, not a symbol.

The uneasy wartime cooperation between the Nationalists (KMT) and the Communists after 1937, following the Xi’an Incident of 1936. A front is not a friendship. It is an agreement about who the enemy is this year.
Sichuan city that became the Nationalist wartime capital after the fall of Nanjing and the retreat up the Yangtze. Japanese bombing of the city, 1938–43, is one of the long air campaigns of the war.
August–November 1937. Urban fighting that made the war visible to foreign concessions and foreign cameras. It did not save Nanjing.

After the city fell in December 1937, Japanese troops killed civilians and disarmed soldiers on a mass scale and committed widespread rape. This capsule names the event and does not illustrate it with bodies.

League of Nations commission, 1931–32, led by Lord Lytton, sent to investigate Japan’s seizure of Manchuria after the Mukden Incident. Its report rejected Japan’s account. Japan left the League. The war of 1937 still came.
18 September 1931: an explosion on the South Manchuria Railway used by the Kwantung Army as a pretext to seize Mukden (Shenyang) and then Manchuria. The before of 1937.
The Nationalist government’s army, commanded in this war by Chiang Kai-shek. Not the only Chinese armed force in the field; the Communists fought as well, under the United Front’s strained roof.
December 1936: Zhang Xueliang detained Chiang Kai-shek in Xi’an to force a turn from civil war toward resistance against Japan. The Second United Front follows. A kidnapping used as policy.
The city now called Beijing. In 1937 it was Beiping — “Northern Peace” — because the Nationalist capital was Nanjing. Names in this capsule follow the political geography of the year.

fun_fact.title: Europeans named the bridge for a traveler
fun_fact.text: The stone bridge at Wanping is 盧溝橋, the Lugou Bridge. Europeans called it the Marco Polo Bridge because Polo’s Travels describe a fine bridge in this region. The 1937 incident entered English under the traveler’s name. The soldiers at Wanping were not fighting over a memoir. They were fighting over a crossing and a railway town. The nickname is a European label that stuck.

sections.title: Japan had already seized Manchuria in 1931

blocks.text: On 18 September 1931 the Kwantung Army used an explosion on the South Manchuria Railway as a pretext to seize Mukden (Shenyang) and then Manchuria. The League of Nations sent the Lytton Commission. The commissioners walked tracks, took testimony, and produced a report that did not accept Japan’s story. Japan left the League. The occupation stayed.

blocks.alt: Men in suits and hats inspecting a railway track in an open landscape.
blocks.caption: Investigators on a Manchurian railway — the kind of scene the Lytton Commission’s 1931–32 inquiry produced. A League report can name a pretext. It could not put the province back.

blocks.text: Inside China the 1930s were also a civil war. The Xi’an Incident of December 1936 — Zhang Xueliang detaining Chiang Kai-shek — forced a turn: a Second United Front against Japan. The front was a cease-fire with a shared enemy, not a merger of the Nationalists and the Communists. That is the politics standing behind 7 July 1937.

sections.title: The 1937 fighting spread from Wanping to Shanghai, Nanjing, and Chongqing

blocks.text: On the night of 7 July 1937 a Japanese unit near the Lugou Bridge claimed a missing soldier and demanded entry to Wanping. Shots followed. The incident did not stay local. By the end of the month Beiping and Tianjin were gone. In August the Battle of Shanghai opened a war that foreign concessions could photograph from their own rooftops. The fighting lasted into November. It did not save Nanjing.

blocks.alt: Chiang Kai-shek in uniform looking through binoculars, other officers behind him.
blocks.caption: Chiang Kai-shek, in the field, looking through binoculars — a wartime command image. The Nationalist state would lose its capital and move the government upriver. The man in the cap is not the whole war. He is the government that had to relocate.

blocks.alt: A man pulling a cart piled with furniture and a child’s rocking horse through a Chinese city street.
blocks.caption: A civilian pulling a household — chairs, boards, a rocking horse — through a city street. The War of Resistance is a military history. It is also this: millions of people walking inland with what a cart would hold.

blocks.text: Nanjing, the capital, fell in December 1937. What followed is the Nanjing Massacre: mass killing of civilians and prisoners, mass rape. This lesson uses one photograph of a city after air attack — rubble, people standing in it, no bodies arranged for the lens. The event does not need a corpse to be believed. If you need numbers, go to the historians who argue over them in public. They are not invented here.

blocks.alt: Civilians standing in a wide field of rubble after the bombing of a Chinese city, 1937.
blocks.caption: A Chinese city after bombing, 1937 — the archive filename places it in Nanjing. People in the frame are standing. This is the one Nanjing image in the lesson: a capital made into a field of rubble, not a gallery of the dead.

blocks.text: The government went to Chongqing. From 1938 the city was bombed, again and again, for years. People lived in tunnels. The wartime capital is not a footnote to the fall of France. It is where the Republic of China was still a state.

blocks.alt: A Japanese twin-engine bomber over a river city, smoke plumes on the ground.
blocks.caption: A Japanese bomber over a river city, smoke on the ground — the archive identifies the campaign against Chongqing. From the air, a capital is a target set. From the ground, it is a schedule of sirens.

blocks.text: In September 1939 Germany invaded Poland. From London that is when “the war” begins. From Chongqing it is the year the European war joined a war already two years old. The United Front still held, badly. Zhou Enlai in the Nationalist capital was diplomacy as much as alliance. Xiao Hong, who had already fled the Northeast, died in 1942 in Japanese-occupied Hong Kong — a writer’s war, not a general’s.

blocks.alt: Zhou Enlai in a dark suit standing between Edgar Snow and Deng Yingchao.
blocks.caption: Zhou Enlai (center) with the American journalist Edgar Snow and Deng Yingchao, 1938. The United Front had to be explained to foreigners as well as fought. A photograph of three people standing is not a merger of two parties.

sections.title: A general, a diplomat, a writer

people.name: Chiang Kai-shek 蔣介石
people.caption: Wartime command photograph, looking through binoculars.
people.text: Head of the Nationalist government and commander of the National Revolutionary Army. He lost the coast and kept a state in Sichuan. The after of 1945 — civil war, then Taiwan — is also his.

people.name: Zhou Enlai 周恩來
people.alt: Zhou Enlai with Edgar Snow and Deng Yingchao.
people.caption: 1938, with Edgar Snow and Deng Yingchao.
people.text: Communist representative in the United Front’s public face. Chongqing and the liaison work are part of how the Chinese Communist Party survived the war as a political fact, not only as a guerrilla force.

people.name: Xiao Hong 蕭紅
people.alt: Portrait of the writer Xiao Hong.
people.caption: Xiao Hong, a 1930s portrait.
people.text: Born in the Northeast. The Field of Life and Death and a short life lived as a refugee — Wuhan, Chongqing, Hong Kong. She died in 1942. A war of resistance is also a war of people who were not in uniform.

sections.title: What a refugee cart was carrying

blocks.text: In the Shanghai refugee photograph the cart is a household turned into a load. The rocking horse is the detail that makes the load a family. This is not a cute war. It is a reminder that “home front” in this war often meant there was no front that stayed put, and home was something you carried.
Europe in 1939 produced its own carts. That does not make 1937 a rehearsal.

sections.title: Japan surrendered in 1945, and the Chinese civil war resumed

blocks.text: Japan surrendered in August 1945. The United Front did not become a peace. The civil war resumed; by 1949 the People’s Republic was proclaimed in Beijing and the Republic of China’s government was on Taiwan. Memory split with the states. In the PRC the War of Resistance is a founding story. In Taiwan it is also a founding story, with different heroes. In Japan the same years are a different argument still.
If a later Friday lesson takes 1945–49, it will not be to tidy this one. It will be because the after is a war of its own.
If a world war is dated from 1939, whose 1937 was demoted to a preface?
